subject: reasoning
question: Six people, C, D, E, X, Y and Z, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order) . Only one person sits between X and D when counted from the left of D. Z sits second to the left of C. Z is an immediate neighbour of E and D. How many people sit between Y and Z when counted from the right of Y?
solution:
Six people, C, D, E, X, Y and Z, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order) .

 
• Only one person sits between X and D when counted from the left of D.
 
• Z sits second to the left of C.
 
• Z is an immediate neighbour of E and D.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2"**
